reasoning_content:
The app dev server runs successfully with a direct `timeout 120`. The `just serve` crash ("code=0, signal=null") occurred because... maybe the nx daemon interference. When I ran `just serve`, the app reported "NX Successfully ran target serve for project app" and exited code 0. That's odd.

Actually the issue: `continuous: true` in the serve target. Maybe with concurrent nx run-many and the daemon, the app target completed. But direct run worked fine.

Anyway, the important thing: containers healthy and seeded; backend API serves 250 paths; meilisearch and keycloak respond. The app dev server works when run directly. The `just serve` orchestrator had the app exit - possibly due to nx daemon transient issue.

Let me try `just serve` again, but perhaps running the dev servers with the orchestrator again will work now that caches are warm. Actually maybe multiple nx processes conflicting. Let me just try again.

Actually, considering the full `just up` (without --detach) is the guide's primary command and would start dev servers as part of it. The task is to "install" - which is really bringing up the dev stack. The stack is up (containers + seed). The dev servers are the frontends.

Let me retry `just serve` in background and check whether all three come up. The first attempt's app "completed" successfully - maybe due to nx daemon race. Let me restart nx daemon first.

Actually, the previous crash may have been caused by my earlier direct-run command interfering? No, the crash was before that.

Let me try running `just serve` again.

action.command:
cd /workspace; nohup env URBO_INSTANCE=urbo just serve > /tmp/justserve2.log 2>&1 &
echo "pid=$!"; sleep 90; tail -12 /tmp/justserve2.log; echo "---endpoints---"; for h in app cms boards; do code=$(curl -sS -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" --resolve "$h.urbo.localhost:80:127.0.0.1" "http://$h.urbo.localhost/"); echo "$h -> $code"; done
